title: About
text:
Hi, I’m Vivek Yadav
I’m a travel demand modeler at Cambridge Systematics. I build and test models that help planning agencies answer several questions.

title: About
text:
How I got into this


KochiCivil engineer on a refinery expansion


BangaloreStudying how pilgrims moved at the Kumbh Mela, at IISc


AtlantaTransportation systems engineering at Georgia Tech


TodayTravel demand models, and what LLMs can do for them


I started out as a civil engineer working on a refinery expansion in Kochi. I then went to the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, where I helped study how people moved around during the Kumbh Mela to understand crowd dynamics. We used survey and GPS data to piece together what pilgrims did during the day: where they went and how long they stayed. From there, I went on to study transportation systems engineering at Georgia Tech.
The settings have changed quite a bit since then, but I still like piecing together what people actually do from the data that we have.

title: About
text:
What I work on
I build and update trip-based, tour-based and activity-based models (ABMs), along with freight and commercial vehicle models. I help planning agencies use these models to understand how people and goods move through a region and how travel might change with new infrastructure, different land use, or changes in policy.
A lot of my work involves processing survey, traffic count and GPS data, then using that information to calibrate and validate models. I also lead project teams and work with agency staff to decide what questions the model needs to answer.

title: About
text:
What I’m exploring now
I’m spending more time with large language models (LLMs) and what they might do for travel demand modeling. One thing I’m exploring is whether they can help with calibration. When a model run looks off, can an AI tool look at the results and suggest what to check next?
Could we use LLMs to represent travel decisions in a different way? And what data would we need to know whether it got the choice right? How do we even calibrate or validate them?
